chunks: Do you feel when the Angel of Death enters a house? Or do you see him when he takes out the life of anyone? Rather, how does he take out the life of an embryo in the womb of his mother? Does he reach it through any part of her body? Or did the spirit respond to his call with the permission of its Lord? Or does he stay with him in the mother’s interior? How can he describe his God, who is unable to describe a creature like himself?

key_terms.بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهَا: With the permission of its Lord

ai.seo_question: How does the Angel of Death take the soul according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali employs a dialectical progression from the sensory invisibility of the Angel of Death to the ontological mystery of the soul's extraction, culminating in a critique of anthropomorphic conceptions of the Divine. This passage underscores the Shia theological emphasis on God's transcendence (tanzih), arguing that if humans cannot comprehend the mechanism of death, they certainly cannot define the Creator who commands it. The rhetorical structure serves to dismantle literalist views of the soul's departure, pointing toward a more nuanced understanding of the spiritual realm.
